subject.title: fix(qa): prove Gateway package self-upgrade via update.run

question: Should this registry-to-registry smoke count as `runtime.update-run` coverage for the reviewed checkout, or must the reviewed package participate in the transition?
rationale: Both designs can provide useful evidence, but only maintainers can define whether the QA taxonomy represents current-head implementation coverage or historical published-package operability.

options.title: Require reviewed-SHA coverage
options.body: Package the reviewed SHA as a pinned source or target in the transition and assert its exact version or artifact identity before retaining `runtime.update-run` coverage.

options.title: Narrow the scenario claim
options.body: Keep the published 2026.4.26-to-latest smoke but classify it as registry package compatibility rather than proof of the reviewed runtime implementation.

recommendation.title: Require reviewed-SHA coverage
recommendation.body: Package the reviewed SHA as a pinned source or target in the transition and assert its exact version or artifact identity before retaining `runtime.update-run` coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to the original shipped QA sentinel and recent QA/release infrastructure decisions.
